## Constrained least squares by an active set (`leastsq_kkt`) {#sec-ch10-kkt}

### Summary

Saturation adjustment and the Newton steps of phase equilibrium must solve a least-squares problem whose unknowns are
bounded: a reaction extent cannot use more of a species than there is. kintera solves
$\min \lVert \mathsf A x - b \rVert$ subject to linear equalities and inequalities with an active-set method. Each
iteration solves the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) system of the currently active constraints. It then drops constraints
whose multiplier has the wrong sign and adds constraints the new solution violates. Two policies share the code. The
general one adds every violated row; the feasible-origin one adds one independent row at a time and is used by the
equilibrium solvers.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** $\min \lVert \mathsf A x - b \rVert$ s.t. $\mathsf C x \le d$, first `neq` rows equalities,
@eq-ch10-kkt-system.

**Data.** $\mathsf A$ ($n_1 \times n_2$), $b$, $\mathsf C$ ($n_3 \times n_2$), $d$; $x$ returned in place of $b$.

**Placement.** `equilibrate_tp`, `equilibrate_uv` (feasible origin); `constrained_newton_step` fallback.

**Activation.** Always; `reg` defaults to 0, `max_iter` is set by the caller.

**Guarantee / limits.** Status 0, 1 (bad input), 2 (no convergence) or 3 (singular or infeasible).

**Evidence.** `test_thermo` (`LeastSquaresKkt*`), `test_alloc_space`; see the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathsf A$, objective matrix [-]; $b$, objective vector; $\mathsf C$, constraint matrix; $d$,
constraint bounds; $x$, unknowns ($n_2$); $\mathcal W$, the active set; $\mathsf C_{\mathcal W}$, $d_{\mathcal W}$, its
rows; $\mu$, the multipliers of the active rows; $\varepsilon$, the machine epsilon of the type; $\rho$, the dual
regularization `reg`. The `reg` is a diagonal perturbation of the multiplier block in scaled KKT units; zero
leaves the block unregularized unless a factorization fails.

### Derivation

For a fixed active set, the stationarity and feasibility conditions of
$\tfrac12 \lVert \mathsf A x - b \rVert^2$ with $\mathsf C_{\mathcal W} x = d_{\mathcal W}$ are

$$
\begin{bmatrix} \mathsf A^{\mathrm T} \mathsf A & \mathsf C_{\mathcal W}^{\mathrm T} \\
\mathsf C_{\mathcal W} & \rho\, \mathsf I \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} x \\ \mu \end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix} \mathsf A^{\mathrm T} b \\ d_{\mathcal W} \end{bmatrix} ,
$$ {#eq-ch10-kkt-system}

with $\rho = 0$ unless regularization is asked for or needed. @eq-ch10-kkt-system is assembled and solved in
`leastsq_kkt_impl` ({{< code src/math/leastsq_kkt.h leastsq_kkt_impl >}}), in scaled units.

The scaling is applied before assembly. Column $j$ of $\mathsf A$ is divided by its largest magnitude $\gamma_j$, and
$b$ by its largest magnitude
$\beta$ (at least 1). A constraint row is then expressed in the scaled unknowns $\tilde x_j = x_j \gamma_j / \beta$
and divided by its own largest magnitude, $d$ included:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\tilde a_{ij} &= a_{ij} / \gamma_j \\
\tilde c_{kj} &= \frac{c_{kj}\, \beta / \gamma_j}{r_k} \\
\tilde d_k &= d_k / r_k \\
r_k &= \max\big(|d_k|, \max_j |c_{kj} \beta / \gamma_j|\big)
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch10-kkt-scaling}

@eq-ch10-kkt-scaling is computed by `kkt_column_scale` and `kkt_row_scale`
({{< code src/math/leastsq_kkt.h kkt_row_scale >}}); the solution is scaled back by $\beta / \gamma_j$ at the end. A
column of zeros keeps scale 1.

After each solve, an active inequality whose multiplier is negative is dropped. The general policy then adds every
inactive row with $\tilde c_k \tilde x - \tilde d_k > 0$. The feasible-origin policy adds only the most violated row
whose scaled form keeps more than $\sqrt{\varepsilon}$ of its 2-norm after projection off the active rows (modified
Gram-Schmidt, twice), in `kkt_orthogonalize` ({{< code src/math/leastsq_kkt.h kkt_orthogonalize >}}). The iteration
stops when the active set no longer changes. The Lagrangian, the four KKT conditions and the meaning of a negative
multiplier are derived in @sec-ch04-active-set. Five steps complete the picture for this solver.

*Step 1: the scaling does not change the answer.* Write $x = \mathsf D y$ with $\mathsf D = \operatorname{diag}
(\beta/\gamma_j)$, so $y_j = \tilde x_j$ above. Then $\mathsf A x - b = \beta(\tilde{\mathsf A} y - b/\beta)$ and
row $k$ of $\mathsf C x \le d$ reads $\sum_j c_{kj}(\beta/\gamma_j) y_j \le d_k$; dividing by $r_k > 0$ gives
$\tilde{\mathsf C} y \le \tilde d$ without changing its direction. The problem in $y$ is

$$
\min_y\ \tfrac12\beta^2\big\lVert\tilde{\mathsf A} y - b/\beta\big\rVert^2
\quad\text{subject to}\quad \tilde{\mathsf C} y \le \tilde d ,
$$ {#eq-ch10-kkt-scaled-problem}

the same objective up to the constant factor $\beta^2$ and the same feasible set mapped by the invertible
$\mathsf D$. Its minimiser is $\mathsf D^{-1}$ times the original one, and `leastsq_kkt_impl` maps back with
$x = \mathsf D y$ at the end. The multipliers change only by positive factors, so their signs, which decide the drops,
are the same.

*Step 2: the block system* is @eq-ch10-kkt-system, the stationarity condition
$\tilde{\mathsf A}^{\mathrm T}(\tilde{\mathsf A} y - \tilde b) + \tilde{\mathsf C}_{\mathcal W}^{\mathrm T}\mu = 0$
together with the active rows held as equalities.

*Step 3: what termination proves.* The loop stops when the working set is the same before and after a pass. Then no
row had $\mu < 0$ (none was dropped). Under the general policy no inactive row was violated either (none was added),
so with the block system termination gives stationarity, primal feasibility, $\mu \ge 0$ and complementarity: a KKT
point. The problem is convex, so a KKT point is a global minimum (@sec-ch04-active-set). The feasible-origin policy
gives less. It never adds a violated row that depends on the working set
({{< code src/math/leastsq_kkt.h leastsq_kkt_impl >}}), and after a regularized solve it re-checks only the active
rows. Status 0 therefore guarantees only the rows that are independent of the working set. The returned $x$ can
violate a dependent row and lie below the constrained optimum, so clipping it, the remedy its doc comment names, gives
a feasible point that is not the optimum in general (Limits; candidate row K41 of the defect
list).[^ch10-kkt-k41]

*Step 4: why the loop can cycle.* The textbook primal active-set method (Nocedal and Wright 2006, Algorithm
16.3)[^ch10-kkt-refs] keeps a feasible iterate, moves toward the working-set minimiser only as far as the first
blocking constraint (a ratio test), and drops one row at a time, so the objective never increases. `leastsq_kkt`
instead jumps to the working-set minimiser in every pass, may be infeasible in between, and both drops and adds in one
pass. Nothing makes the objective monotone, so a sequence of working sets can repeat. `max_iter` is the only guard,
and running out is reported as status 2, not silent. The check finds cycling under both policies, and a reach check on
the in-tree decks finds it under the feasible-origin policy that `equilibrate_tp` and `equilibrate_uv` use:
`tests/jupiter.yaml` gives status 2 in 1 of 5000 fixed-$T,p$ states and 2 of 5000 fixed-$U,V$ states between 100
and 105 K, with ammonia gas absent and both ammonia condensates present, still at `max_iter` 1000.[^ch10-kkt-k19]

*Step 5: the regularized retry.* If the block fails to factor, the second attempt adds $\delta$ to the primal
diagonal and $-\delta$ to the dual diagonal. When $\tilde{\mathsf A}^{\mathrm T}\tilde{\mathsf A} + \delta\mathsf I$ is positive definite and the dual block is
$-\delta\mathsf I$, the matrix is quasi-definite, which makes it nonsingular (Vanderbei 1995), so the pivoted LU of the
retry succeeds in exact arithmetic. Because the solution then solves a perturbed problem, the active rows (all rows under
the general policy) are checked afterwards to $64\varepsilon + 10\delta$ (status 3 if they fail).

`check_ch10_dense.py` compares both policies with a brute-force enumeration of active sets:[^ch10-kkt-check]

- "(h1) leastsq_kkt (general), 60 random 6x4 problems with 5 inequalities (x = 0 feasible): status counts {0: 57, 2:
  3}; converged cases: max rel diff to brute-force optimum 2.4e-15 (tol 1e-9) PASS"
- "(h2) KKT residuals of those results: stationarity 2.0e-15, dual infeasibility 0.0e+00, complementarity 8.2e-15,
  primal infeasibility 8.9e-16 (tol 1e-9) PASS"
- "(h4) column scaling 1e-6..1e8 and row scaling 1e-7..1e5: status 0,0, rel diff 1.6e-16 (tol 1e-9) PASS"
- "(h5) iteration cap: full run status 0 in 3 iterations; with max_iter=1 status 2 (2 expected when more than 1
  iteration is needed) PASS"
- "(h1c) the 3 non-converged problems rerun with max_iter=1000: statuses [2, 2, 2], distance of the returned x to the
  optimum 0.22, 2.29, 0.02 (every convex problem with x = 0 feasible should converge) EXPECTED-FAIL (S10-4: active-set
  cycling)", row K19 of the defect list
- "(i1c) the 1 non-converged problems rerun with max_iter=1000: statuses [2] EXPECTED-FAIL (S10-5: active-set cycling,
  policy used by equilibrate_tp/uv)", row K19
- "(i3) single-coefficient active row: x_0 = 0.3 (bound 0.3 exactly) PASS"

**The direct square form.** For square nonsingular $\tilde{\mathsf A}$, multiply the first block row of
@eq-ch10-kkt-system by $\tilde{\mathsf A}^{-\mathrm T}$:
$\tilde{\mathsf A}^{-\mathrm T}\tilde{\mathsf A}^{\mathrm T}\tilde{\mathsf A}\,y +
\tilde{\mathsf A}^{-\mathrm T}\tilde{\mathsf C}_{\mathcal W}^{\mathrm T}\mu =
\tilde{\mathsf A}^{-\mathrm T}\tilde{\mathsf A}^{\mathrm T}\tilde b$, that is

$$
\begin{bmatrix} \tilde{\mathsf A} & \tilde{\mathsf A}^{-\mathrm T}\tilde{\mathsf C}_{\mathcal W}^{\mathrm T} \\
\tilde{\mathsf C}_{\mathcal W} & \rho\,\mathsf I \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} y \\ \mu \end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix} \tilde b \\ \tilde d_{\mathcal W} \end{bmatrix} .
$$ {#eq-ch10-kkt-direct}

The second block row is unchanged, and the first was multiplied by an invertible matrix, so @eq-ch10-kkt-direct has
exactly the solutions $(y, \mu)$ of @eq-ch10-kkt-system. It contains $\tilde{\mathsf A}$ instead of
$\tilde{\mathsf A}^{\mathrm T}\tilde{\mathsf A}$, so its conditioning follows $\operatorname{cond}(\tilde{\mathsf A})$,
not its square. `kkt_solve_direct` factors $\tilde{\mathsf A}^{\mathrm T}$ once, forms the columns
$\tilde{\mathsf A}^{-\mathrm T}\tilde c_k^{\mathrm T}$ by back substitution, and factors the block.
`check_ch10_dense.py`: "(i1) leastsq_kkt_feasible_origin, 60 random square problems, 5 generic inequalities, d >= 0:
status counts {0: 59, 2: 1}; converged cases: max rel diff to brute force 5.2e-14 (tol 1e-9) PASS".

### Numerical method

1. Inputs are checked: $n_1 \ge n_2 > 0$, $n_3 \ge 0$, $0 \le$ `neq` $\le n_3$; otherwise status 1.
2. The feasible-origin policy also checks that $x = 0$ is feasible: $d_k \ge -64 \varepsilon \max|d|$ on inequalities
   and $|d_k| \le 64 \varepsilon \max|d|$ on equalities; otherwise status 1 and the input array of $b$ unchanged.
3. Each iteration first tries, under the feasible-origin policy and for square $\mathsf A$, the direct form
   $[[\mathsf A_s, \mathsf A_s^{-\mathrm T} \mathsf C_s^{\mathrm T}], [\mathsf C_s, \rho \mathsf I]]$ in
   `kkt_solve_direct` ({{< code src/math/leastsq_kkt.h kkt_solve_direct >}}). Its conditioning follows that of
   $\mathsf A$, not its square; the derivation is in the Derivation layer above.
4. Otherwise, or if that fails, the normal-equation block @eq-ch10-kkt-system is factored with `ludcmp` at pivot
   tolerance $10 \varepsilon$. All-zero rows are skipped, and an all-zero row with a nonzero right-hand side gives
   status 3. If the factorization fails, a second attempt adds $10^{-10}$ ($10^{-5}$ in single precision) to the
   primal diagonal, and $-10^{-10}$ to the dual diagonal when $\rho = 0$.
5. If regularization was used, the final active rows must hold, and under the general policy every row must hold,
   to $64 \varepsilon + 10 \times$ the fallback value; otherwise status 3.
6. The feasible-origin policy returns an unknown bounded by an active single-coefficient row exactly on its bound,
   $x_j = d_k / c_{kj}$.
7. Reaching `max_iter` without a fixed active set prints a warning and returns 2; `max_iter` is overwritten with the
   iterations used.

Scratch space comes from the `work` pool, sized by `leastsq_kkt_space` and `leastsq_kkt_feasible_origin_space`
({{< code src/utils/alloc.h leastsq_kkt_space >}}). The figure of the active-set swaps is not provided: the figure
module is not written yet; the code carries it as an ASCII diagram.

: Code map of the constrained least-squares solver. {#tbl-ch10-kkt-code}

The feasible-origin policy is called by `equilibrate_tp` ({{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_tp.h >}}) and
`equilibrate_uv` ({{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_uv.h >}}); the general policy runs as the fallback of
`constrained_newton_step` (@sec-ch10-newton).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_thermo` | general policy, 12 cases: solution, status, iterations | $10^{-12}$ to $10^{-6}$ abs., $10^{-10}$ rel., or exact | the test |
| `test_thermo` | feasible-origin policy, 6 cases: dependent rows, exact bounds | $10^{-18}$ to $10^{-5}$ abs., or exact | the test |
| `test_alloc_space` | both policies stay inside their pool budget | guard intact | the test |

: Tests of the constrained least-squares solver. {#tbl-ch10-kkt-tests}

The cases are in {{< code tests/test_thermo.cpp >}} and {{< code tests/test_alloc_space.cpp >}}. The general
policy's cases form the gtest suite `LeastSquaresKkt` and the feasible-origin cases the suite
`LeastSquaresKktFeasibleOrigin`. Examples: a redundant pair of equalities is solved with regularization to
$10^{-8}$ (case `RegularizesRedundantActiveConstraints` of the first suite). An inconsistent pair returns status 3
and leaves $x = 0$ (case `RejectsInconsistentEqualities`). A $-10^{-19}$ round-off bound is accepted as feasible to
$10^{-18}$ (case `AcceptsRoundOffNegativeBound` of the second suite). The cases of the first suite are plain gtest
cases on the CPU; two of them go through `constrained_newton_step`. The CUDA path of the same template is reached
only through the `DeviceTest` equilibrium cases of `test_thermo`, which are also instantiated for CUDA. No run
record is attached in this draft (missing evidence).

### Limits

- The error message for a bad `neq` says "must be non-negative" also when `neq` exceeds $n_3$.
- The active-set iteration can cycle on convex problems with a feasible origin (step 4), under both policies;
  `max_iter` is the only guard (status 2). The in-tree deck `tests/jupiter.yaml` reaches it (row K19).
- The feasible-origin policy may return, with status 0, an $x$ that violates a dependent row it chose not to activate
  and lies below the constrained optimum (step 3); the caller must clip the step, as its doc comment states
  ({{< code src/math/leastsq_kkt.h leastsq_kkt_feasible_origin >}}), and the clipped step is not the optimum in
  general (candidate row K41).
- `reg` is a `float` argument even when `T` is `double`.
